documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from December. With wife. No new problems. Memory about the same per wife, keeps busy with yard plans for spring and church on weekends. Takes meds from the weekly box she fills. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no swelling.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear.
A/P: HTN at goal on current regimen. Lipids and BMP today. Alzheimer's stable on donepezil. Glaucoma stable per November letter. Next visit summer for AWV.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is his wife. The mail order says the amlodipine prescription ran out of refills. Can you renew it?

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Renewed amlodipine 5 mg, 90 days with 3 refills, to the mail order pharmacy this morning.

conditions.label: ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction involving right coronary artery

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 110. ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF.

Portable AP chest. Bilateral perihilar and basilar airspace opacities with interstitial thickening and vascular congestion. Cardiac silhouette at upper limits of normal for technique. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, visit 05/26/2022, received by fax.

69-year-old man brought by ambulance. About two hours before arrival he became acutely short of breath while cutting the grass, with palpitations and inability to lie flat. Denies chest pain. History: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, open-angle glaucoma, Alzheimer's dementia. No known coronary disease. NKDA.

Triage: BP 150/90, HR 110, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air.
Exam: in respiratory distress, speaking in short phrases. Crackles to the mid lung fields bilaterally. JVD present. New holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating toward the axilla. No leg edema.
ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF. Troponin I 10 ng/mL (reference <0.04). Portable chest film with pulmonary edema.

Course: STEMI alert at 16:52. Aspirin 324 mg chewed, heparin bolus, IV furosemide, noninvasive ventilation. Cardiology at bedside; to the cath lab at 17:55.
Diagnoses: acute inferior STEMI; acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema.

documents.title: Discharge summary: inferior STEMI
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admitted 05/26/2022, discharged 05/29/2022.

Principal diagnosis: acute inferior ST-elevation MI. Secondary: acute decompensated heart failure, resolved; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; HIV on ART; Alzheimer's dementia; primary open-angle glaucoma.

Catheterization 05/26: right radial access. Right coronary artery occluded in its mid segment, culprit. Left main, LAD and circumflex without significant stenosis. Thrombectomy not needed; one drug-eluting stent to the mid RCA with TIMI 3 flow restored. No complications.
Course: diuresed overnight, off noninvasive ventilation by the next morning, on room air from day 2. Telemetry without sustained arrhythmia. Walked the halls on day 3 without symptoms.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; clopidogrel 75 mg daily (new, for at least 12 months after the stent); metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; Biktarvy daily; latanoprost both eyes nightly; donepezil 10 mg daily. NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiology 6-8 weeks; PCP 1-2 weeks. Return for chest pain or breathlessness.

documents.title: Wife calling: hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called to let us know he was taken to the regional hospital yesterday afternoon with trouble breathing and was found to be having a heart attack; a stent was placed last evening. He is in the cardiac unit, breathing easier this morning. Requested records be sent. Will book a hospital follow-up once discharge date is known. PCP notified.

events.reason: Sudden dyspnea, chest pain and palpitations after recent MI

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 122. Q waves in II, III and aVF, unchanged from the discharge tracing. No new ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Sinus tachycardia; evolving inferior infarct pattern without new acute change.

reports.text: Limited bedside study. Dilated left ventricle. Color flow demonstrates a jet across the interventricular septum consistent with a ventricular septal defect with left-to-right shunting.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 05/31/2022.

Returned five days after admission for inferior STEMI with RCA stent; discharged two days ago on aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol and atorvastatin with his usual medicines. This morning at rest he developed sudden breathlessness, chest pain and a racing heartbeat.

Vitals: BP 85/50, HR 122, RR 28.
Exam: diaphoretic, distressed. Rales at both bases. Loud harsh holosystolic murmur at the left sternal border with a palpable thrill. JVP elevated.
Labs: troponin I elevated; BNP markedly elevated; creatinine 1.2 (baseline 1.0); hemoglobin 13.2; WBC 12,000.
ECG: inferior Q waves, as on discharge. Bedside echo: dilated LV with flow across the ventricular septum.

Assessment: post-infarction ventricular septal rupture with cardiogenic shock.
Course: vasopressor support started, cardiothoracic surgery consulted, transferred to the tertiary cardiac surgery center at 10:20.

documents.title: Discharge summary: VSD repair
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Tertiary cardiac surgery center. Admitted 05/31/2022 in transfer, discharged 06/13/2022 home with services.

Diagnosis: post-infarction ventricular septal defect after inferior STEMI (RCA stent 05/26/2022), with cardiogenic shock and acute decompensated heart failure.

Operation 06/01/2022: surgical patch repair of the inferoseptal ventricular septal defect on cardiopulmonary bypass. Intraoperative TEE after repair: no residual shunt. Clopidogrel held before surgery and resumed on postoperative day 3.
Postoperative course: extubated day 1, vasopressors weaned by day 3, chest tubes out day 4. Diuresed to dry weight. Ambulating independently at discharge.
Discharge exam: sternal wound clean. No murmur. Lungs clear. Weight 82.0 kg.
Labs at discharge: creatinine back to 1.0, hemoglobin 12.5.

Discharge medications: unchanged from the 05/29 list: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20 (restarted day 6 once pressures recovered), amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost, donepezil 10. NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiac surgery wound check 2 weeks; cardiology 6 weeks with echo; PCP within 1 week; cardiac rehab referral at cardiology visit. Sternal precautions 8 weeks.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after STEMI and VSD repair

documents.title: Transitional care visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 3 days after discharge; RN reached the family by phone on 06/14. Wife and daughter present.

Two admissions in three weeks: inferior STEMI 05/26 with RCA drug-eluting stent (presented with pulmonary edema), then on 05/31 a post-infarction VSD with shock, repaired surgically 06/01 at the tertiary center. Both discharge summaries reviewed.

Today: tired but walking around the house and to the mailbox. Mild sternal soreness. No chest pressure like before, no orthopnea, sleeping flat on two pillows (his usual). No palpitations. Appetite returning. Family says he is at his usual baseline.

Med reconciliation done with the bottles: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75 (new), metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost, donepezil 10. Wife has the pill box set.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP soft-normal. Sternotomy healing, no drainage. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Weight 82.0 kg, matches discharge.

A/P
1. Inferior STEMI s/p RCA DES; post-infarction VSD s/p patch repair; recent decompensated heart failure, resolved. Doing well. Dual antiplatelet therapy for at least 12 months; stressed not stopping clopidogrel without cardiology. Sternal precautions. Daily weights, call for gain of 3 lb in a day or 5 in a week. BMP and CBC today.
2. HTN: at the low end on full regimen; if lightheaded, hold amlodipine and call.
3. Alzheimer's: family supervision continues.
4. Cardiology and cardiac surgery follow-ups are scheduled.
RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Labs from Thursday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium are normal. His blood count is a little low, which is expected a few weeks after heart surgery, and should recover on its own; we'll recheck at the next visit. No changes. Keep up the daily weights and let us know if they creep up.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Seen 07/19/2022 with his daughter, 7 weeks after inferior STEMI with mid-RCA DES and 6 weeks after surgical repair of a post-infarction VSD. Cleared at his surgical wound check. Walking 15 minutes twice a day, no angina, no dyspnea at that level, no palpitations.
Exam: BP and pulse well controlled; sternum healed; regular rhythm, no murmur; lungs clear; no edema.
Plan: continue aspirin and clopidogrel through at least 05/2023; metoprolol, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril and amlodipine unchanged. Echo in 3 weeks. Referral to cardiac rehabilitation sent. Return in one year, sooner if needed.

reports.text: Complete study. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness. Hypokinesis of the inferior wall; remaining segments contract normally. LVEF 55% by biplane method. Patch in the inferior septum intact with no residual shunt by color flow. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Trace mitral regurgitation; papillary muscles intact. Other valves normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Intact VSD patch without residual shunt. LVEF 55% with inferior wall hypokinesis.

documents.title: Echo reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Outside echo: patch intact, no leak, EF 55%. Good news, shared with daughter by portal.

conditions.label: ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction involving right coronary artery

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, three months after the MI and VSD repair. Started cardiac rehab last week, three mornings a week; daughter drives him. Feels his stamina coming back. No chest pain, no breathlessness walking on flat ground. Echo this month: EF 55%, patch intact.
Function: needs prompting for bathing, otherwise independent in basic ADLs; family manages meds and finances. No falls. PHQ-9 4, mostly low energy since surgery.

Exam: vitals as charted. Sternotomy well healed. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
- Old inferior MI, CAD s/p RCA DES, VSD s/p repair: on aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol, atorvastatin, lisinopril, amlodipine. Rehab underway. Lipids today.
- Alzheimer's on donepezil; health care proxy on file (daughter).
- Glaucoma, HIV: stable, followed outside.
- Prevention: lung CT in September, flu and bivalent COVID in October.
RTC 5 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT, comparison 09/2021. Interval median sternotomy with intact wires. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Coronary stent noted in the right coronary artery.

documents.title: LDCT 2022
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lung-RADS 1. Post-surgical changes only. Repeat next year.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza R deltoid, Moderna bivalent booster L deltoid. Daughter present. Tolerated without issue. Next AWV booked.

documents.title: Cardiac rehabilitation discharge summary
documents.author: cardiac rehabilitation
documents.body: Phase II cardiac rehabilitation completed 08/16/2022 to 10/20/2022, 30 of 36 sessions attended. No angina or arrhythmia during monitored exercise. Exercise tolerance improved from 2.8 to 4.6 METs. Home walking program given. Family educated on heart-healthy eating. Discharged from program.

documents.title: Infectious disease annual note
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body: HIV visit 11/15/2022. Interval STEMI with stent and VSD repair noted; we reviewed his new cardiac medicines and there are no significant interactions with bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF. Viral load not detected, CD4 580 cells/mm3. Continue ART. Return in one year.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Glaucoma visit 12/06/2022. Wife giving latanoprost nightly. IOP 18 right, 17 left. Fields stable compared with last year. Discs unchanged. Continue latanoprost. One year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Finished cardiac rehab in October and keeps walking in the mall on cold days. No chest pain, dyspnea or palpitations. Taking clopidogrel and aspirin, no bleeding.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: CAD after inferior MI and VSD repair, stable on DAPT, beta blocker, statin, ACE inhibitor. HTN controlled. BMP today. Alzheimer's stable per family. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail order asking for clopidogrel renewal; original hospital prescription out of refills. Per cardiology plan, at least 12 months from 05/2022. Sent 90-day supply with 1 refill; cardiology to decide on stopping at their summer visit.

conditions.label: Cerebral infarction due to unspecified occlusion or stenosis of right anterior cerebral artery

reports.text: Noncontrast head CT. Hypodensity with loss of gray-white differentiation in the right paramedian frontal and parietal lobes in the anterior cerebral artery territory. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Acute infarct in the right anterior cerebral artery territory. No hemorrhage.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 05/18/2023.

70-year-old man brought in by his wife, who saw him scuffing his left foot along the floor this afternoon. He has no pain and says the leg just will not lift right. Background: CAD with inferior MI and RCA stent 05/2022, post-MI VSD repaired, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, Alzheimer's dementia, glaucoma. No previous stroke or TIA. On aspirin and clopidogrel. NKDA.

Exam: alert and oriented. Cranial nerves intact. Strength 5/5 in both arms and the right leg; left leg 3/5 with mildly increased tone. Sensation intact. Coordination and reflexes normal in the upper extremities.
CT head: acute right ACA territory infarct, no hemorrhage.

Impression: acute ischemic stroke, right anterior cerebral artery territory, first event. Admitted to the stroke unit.

documents.title: Discharge summary: ischemic stroke
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 05/18/2023, discharged 05/21/2023 home with wife.

Diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, right anterior cerebral artery territory, presenting with left leg weakness.
Course: neuro checks stable, no worsening. Continuous telemetry showed sinus rhythm throughout. Evaluated by physical therapy: safe for home with a rolling walker short term; outpatient PT arranged. Left leg strength 3+/5 at discharge, walking with walker and standby assist.
Medications: no changes. Continue aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost, donepezil 10. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; outpatient PT; neurology in 3 months; cardiology as scheduled.

orders.reason: Left leg weakness after right ACA stroke

documents.title: Transitional care visit after stroke
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit with wife and daughter, 4 days after discharge for a right ACA territory stroke presenting as left leg weakness. ED record and discharge summary reviewed. RN call on 05/22 documented.

Since home: walking in the house with the rolling walker, wife next to him on stairs. No falls. Leg feels a bit stronger. No new weakness, speech or vision change. Mood okay.
Meds reconciled, unchanged.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, follows commands, at his cognitive baseline per family. Left hip flexion and ankle dorsiflexion 4-/5, right side 5/5, arms 5/5. Walks with walker, mild left foot drag.

A/P
1. Right ACA stroke, first event, on aspirin plus clopidogrel at the time. Hospital kept DAPT unchanged; cardiology visit in July will address clopidogrel duration. Outpatient PT referral placed today (hospital referral had not reached the PT office). Fall precautions at home.
2. CAD, HTN, HLD: unchanged.
3. Alzheimer's: no acute change.
RTC after PT and at AWV in August.

documents.title: Physical therapy initial evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body: Outpatient PT evaluation 06/01/2023. Referral: right ACA stroke 05/18/2023 with left leg weakness. Wife assists with history. Left hip flexion and knee extension 4-/5, ankle dorsiflexion 4-/5; right leg and both arms full strength. Gait with rolling walker, decreased left foot clearance. Plan: twice weekly for 8-10 weeks, strengthening, gait and balance training, home exercise program supervised by family. Goal: walk without device in the community.

medications.reason: Completed 14 months of dual antiplatelet therapy after DES

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Seen 07/18/2023, 14 months after inferior STEMI with mid-RCA DES and VSD repair. Interval right ACA stroke in May while on dual antiplatelet therapy; telemetry sinus throughout. Now in outpatient PT, walking with a cane. No angina, dyspnea or palpitations.
Exam: BP and pulse controlled; regular rhythm; no murmur; lungs clear; no edema.
Plan: dual antiplatelet therapy is complete; stop clopidogrel, continue aspirin 81 mg indefinitely. Continue metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5. Return in one year.

documents.title: Physical therapy discharge summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body: Discharged from outpatient PT after 18 visits (06/01-08/10/2023). Left leg strength now 5/5 throughout. Gait normal without assistive device, including stairs with one rail. Goals met. Continue home exercise program with wife.

conditions.label: Cerebral infarction due to unspecified occlusion or stenosis of right anterior cerebral artery
History of stroke without residual deficits

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with daughter. Finished PT last week: left leg back to full strength, walking without a cane. Cardiology stopped clopidogrel in July, aspirin continues. No chest pain or breathlessness. Neurology visit next week.
Function: walks independently, dresses himself, needs cues for bathing; family manages meds, money, appointments. No falls since May. PHQ-9 3.

Exam: vitals as charted. Strength 5/5 all four limbs. Gait normal, turns steadily. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
- Stroke in May, full recovery: now history of stroke without residual deficits. Aspirin, statin, BP control.
- CAD after inferior MI, VSD repaired: stable.
- Alzheimer's on donepezil: neurology next week.
- Labs today. Lung CT next month. Fall vaccines: flu, updated COVID, and the new RSV vaccine.
RTC 5 months.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Follow-up 08/22/2023 with daughter. Right ACA infarct in May with left leg weakness, now fully recovered after PT. Cognition: family describes a small step down since the stroke, more help needed with planning. MMSE 18/30 (20/30 in 2021). Neuro exam nonfocal; gait normal. Continue donepezil 10 mg. Family support and day structure discussed. Return in 18 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT, comparison 09/2022. Stable postoperative sternotomy changes. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, effusion or adenopathy.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three vaccines per PCP plan after shared decision at AWV: high-dose flu L deltoid, updated COVID R deltoid, RSV L deltoid 1 inch below. Daughter present and consented with patient. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Infectious disease annual note
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body: HIV visit 11/14/2023. Stroke in May noted, recovered. Adherence excellent with family support. CD4 620 cells/mm3, viral load not detected. Continue bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF. One year.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Seen 12/05/2023. Latanoprost nightly. IOP 17 right, 18 left. Visual fields stable, discs stable. Continue current drop. Return in one year.
